turns.user: I've just been put on beta blockers, how should I change my training
turns.reply:
Beta blockers will cap your heart rate, which means using a heart rate monitor to judge your intensity isn't going to work anymore—your heart literally won't be able to pump as fast, even when you're working hard. 

First, you need to clear this with your doctor or pharmacist to make sure they are happy with you continuing to lift, as they can advise on your specific dosage and cardiovascular health. 

Once you have their green light, the best way to change your training is to switch from tracking heart rate to using RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion) on a 1-to-10 scale. We'll judge your effort by how hard the muscles are working and how heavy the weight feels, rather than what a watch says. You should also take longer rest periods between sets and transition slowly from lying or sitting exercises to standing up, as beta blockers can sometimes make you feel a bit dizzy if you stand up too fast.

Have you had a chance to speak with your doctor about training on them yet?

turns.user: I know you can't prescribe, just tell me roughly what to expect
turns.reply:
Expect your heart rate to stay noticeably lower than usual, even when you're working hard or feeling out of breath—that's just the medication doing its job by keeping that ceiling on your heart rate. 

Because of that, you might feel like you hit a "wall" or run out of steam a bit faster than normal, especially during anything fast-paced or high-rep. Your body is just adapting to a slightly restricted oxygen delivery system during intense work. You might also notice a bit of mild dizziness if you stand up too quickly after a heavy set, so taking an extra thirty seconds to sit up before standing is a smart habit to build. 

Are you currently doing any cardio in your routine, or are we mostly looking at how this affects your lifting?
